provinces.name: Ontario
story_threads: Honda indefinitely suspended its $15B Ontario EV and battery investment (Alliston); the four near-duplicate Honda ON records in projects_all.json are tagged Cancelled and excluded from the active pipeline, so the suspended ~$15B is not counted toward the province's active capital value.

Ontario's tracked pipeline holds 728 projects with ~$360B in stated value (Cancelled Honda entries included in the raw aggregate); infrastructure leads with 31 valued projects (~$123B) including the $27.4B Ontario Line and $26.1B GO Expansion.

Ontario unemployment is 7.5% (April 2026 LFS), above the national 6.9%; Ontario Budget 2026 projects the provincial rate easing from 7.7% (2025) to 7.4% (2026) and a $210B ten-year capital plan tied to 412 tracked projects.

Ontario CPI is +2.9% YoY, the highest among the four largest provinces, while provincial GDP growth is +1.2%; provincial economic accounts (most recent available, Q3 2025) show exports $638,705M (+4.3%) and goods GDP $177,899M (-1.5%).

cross_references.interpretation: Elevated unemployment coincides with a large infrastructure-led pipeline; Ontario Budget 2026's $210B capital plan is linked to 412 tracked projects.

provinces.name: Quebec
story_threads: Quebec employment fell 43,300 in April 2026 (-0.9%), with cumulative 2026 losses near 87,000 jobs; about half concentrated in construction and manufacturing, roughly one quarter in financial services; unemployment rose to 6.2%.

Quebec's tracked pipeline holds 520 projects with ~$78.4B in stated value; power/energy leads with 29 valued projects (~$35.4B), followed by mining (23 projects, ~$19.9B) and infrastructure (17 projects, ~$18.1B).

Quebec CPI is -0.4% YoY (lowest among provinces), while provincial GDP growth is +1.3%; the construction/manufacturing job losses align with the construction-heavy infrastructure pipeline (Blue Line extension, TramCité, REM branches).

Quebec Budget 2026-27 carries a $167B infrastructure plan linked to 289 tracked projects; provincial accounts (most recent available, Q3 2025) show real GDP $486,872.74M (-0.1%) and exports $208,930M (+0.2%).

cross_references.interpretation: Construction and manufacturing absorbed roughly half the losses; the province's pipeline is construction-intensive (infrastructure $18.1B, 17 projects).

provinces.name: Alberta
story_threads: ATB raised Alberta's 2026 real GDP forecast to 2.7% (from 2.1%) and nominal GDP to +6%, citing higher oil prices and a WTI 2026 forecast near US$75/bbl; indicators.json carries provincial GDP growth at +2.7%.

Alberta's tracked pipeline holds 733 projects with ~$346.9B in stated value; power/energy leads with 74 valued projects (~$137.3B), followed by manufacturing (17 projects, ~$65.8B) and oil_gas (16 projects, ~$44.4B).
Alberta unemployment is 7.0% (April 2026), in line with national; one report projects the fiscal position could swing from a ~$9.4B deficit to a ~$6B surplus if elevated oil prices are sustained.

The Canada-Alberta Co-operation Agreement on environmental/impact assessment (signed Apr 2, 2026) caps assessment timelines at two years; the Flipi Gas-Fired Generation Project (460 MW, TransAlta) was Approved via IAAC early decision (64-day review).

provinces.name: Newfoundland and Labrador
story_threads: Equinor submitted the Bay du Nord development application to Newfoundland and Labrador's energy regulator in early May 2026; the March 2026 provincial agreement provides up to $6.4B in direct provincial revenue in phase one, with project investment ~$14B and first oil ~2031.

Newfoundland and Labrador's tracked pipeline holds 1,561 projects with ~$25.8B in stated value; power/energy leads with 7 valued projects (~$16.5B), anchored by Grassy Point LNG ($10B) and White Rose Expansion ($3.8B + $2.3B).

Newfoundland and Labrador unemployment is 10.0% (highest among provinces) and the employment rate 51.6% (lowest); April LFS showed employment -5,200 (-2.1%), the largest single-month percentage decline among provinces.
Offshore oil/gas sustains ~20,000 jobs, ~20% of provincial GDP and ~55% of exports; provincial GDP growth is +2.4% and CPI +2.3% YoY.

provinces.name: Prince Edward Island
story_threads: PEI's 2026 budget (tabled Apr 14) sets a five-year capital plan totaling $1.6B; the FY2026/27 deficit is pegged at $409.9M (~3.5% of GDP), with a new personal income tax bracket above $200,000.

PEI's tracked pipeline holds 82 projects with ~$1.5B in stated value (the smallest provincial pipeline); power/energy leads with 13 valued projects (~$0.6B) and infrastructure adds ~$0.5B across 39 projects.
PEI unemployment is 8.0% and CPI is +4.0% YoY (the highest provincial CPI); provincial GDP growth is +3.6% (the highest provincial GDP growth).
Nominal GDP is assumed +4% (2026/2027) and real GDP +2%, down from ~2.4% (2025); the budget focuses on health care, affordability and energy security.

cross_references.interpretation: Elevated CPI accompanies the highest provincial GDP growth (+3.6%); the pipeline is small and infrastructure/energy-led.
The 39-project infrastructure pipeline (~$0.5B) aligns with the provincial capital plan.

provinces.name: Yukon
story_threads: Yukon tabled a $2.46B 2026-27 budget ($2.07B operations, $385M capital) with an $81.8M deficit; capital spending falls as the Nisutlin Bay Bridge replacement and Whitehorse airport runway projects wind down.

Yukon's tracked pipeline holds 123 projects with ~$46.4B in stated value; a single proposed $40B Northern Defence and Infrastructure Investment dominates, with mining (4 valued projects, ~$4.6B) and 54 infrastructure projects (~$1.0B) behind it.

Yukon unemployment is 5.3% with an employment rate of 71.2% (the highest among all jurisdictions); territorial GDP is -3.3% (2024, latest available — StatCan does not publish CPI or housing starts for territories).
The Canada-Yukon Workforce Tariff Response provides $1.5M over three years for tariff-affected construction, transportation and mining workers/employers.

cross_references.interpretation: Territorial GDP latest is 2024 annual; the pipeline is dominated by a single proposed $40B defence/infrastructure record and placer-gold-linked mining.

provinces.name: Northwest Territories
story_threads: The NWT diamond industry is contracting: Rio Tinto plans to close Diavik in March 2026 (reserves exhausted); Gahcho Kue continues to 2031. The three operating mines directly/indirectly employ >1,500 residents and account for ~one-fifth of NWT GDP.

NWT's tracked pipeline holds 182 projects with ~$40.1B in stated value, dominated by a single proposed $35B Arctic Defence and Infrastructure Spending Package; mining (5 valued projects, ~$2.0B) and 53 infrastructure projects (~$1.2B) follow.
NWT unemployment is 6.8% with an employment rate of 66.1%; territorial GDP is -1.1% (2024, latest available — StatCan does not publish CPI or housing starts for territories).

GNWT released a geological assessment of 1,721 mineral showings across 19 critical minerals (lithium, cobalt, copper, zinc) as a diversification path, with commercial attractiveness contingent on higher prices.

cross_references.interpretation: Diamond-industry contraction (Diavik closure Mar 2026) removes part of the >1,500 diamond-sector jobs (~one-fifth of NWT GDP).
The 5 valued mining projects (~$2.0B) and critical-minerals diversification depend on substantially higher prices.

provinces.name: Nunavut
story_threads: PM Carney referred the Grays Bay Road and Port project (deepwater export terminal plus airstrip, dual-use civilian/military) to the Major Projects Office on Mar 12, 2026; CanNor announced over $13M for four Nunavut projects in April 2026.
Nunavut's tracked pipeline holds 47 projects with ~$2B in stated value; mining leads with a single valued project (B2Gold Back River Gold, $0.61B) and infrastructure adds ~$0.6B across 13 projects.

Nunavut unemployment is 12.0% (the highest among all jurisdictions) and the employment rate is 55.0% (the lowest); territorial GDP is +7.5% (2024, latest available — StatCan does not publish CPI or housing starts for territories).

CanNor funding includes $4.5M to West Kitikmeot Resources for Grays Bay environmental/feasibility studies and $1.1M for an Iqaluit economic-development hub; Canada-Nunavut joint funding of $2.45M supports Baffin Island critical-mineral research.

cross_references.interpretation: The smallest jurisdictional pipeline (47 projects, ~$2B); Grays Bay referral and CanNor funding sit upstream of future capital.
